newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU meeting did not discuss EMU delay - Quinn.
newsitem.headline: EU meeting did not discuss EMU delay - Quinn.

text.p: European Union finance ministers meeting for a two-day informal session in the Netherlands did not discuss the possibility of delaying the scheduled January 1999 start of economic and monetary union, Irish minister Ruairi Quinn told reporters.
Asked whether there had been any talk among ministers of a possible delay to EMU's launch, Quinn said: "None."
Quinn also said ministers had not discussed possible conversion rates for existing currencies and the planned new euro.

Uncertainty over Germany's ability to put its public finances in order in 1997 -- the critical year for those wishing to join the single currency club -- has prompted intense speculation that EMU's 1999 start-date might have to be delayed.
Bonn's budget problems have been compounded by record unemployment and a political backdrop of widening labour unrest and public hostility to a common currency.
Germany's participation in the first wave of EMU is seen as critical to the project's viability.
